nodes.description: External function disperseTokenSimple(IERC20,address[3],uint256[3]) that loops over recipients and pulls tokens from msg.sender via transferFrom, multiplying each value by 10**18.
Parameter token of type IERC20: the token contract on which the external transferFrom call is executed.
Parameter recipients: fixed-size address[3] array of destination addresses receiving the dispersed tokens.
Parameter values: fixed-size uint256[3] array of amounts that are scaled by 10**18 before transfer.
Loop counter i (uint256) used to index recipients[i] and values[i] while iterating over the arrays.
msg.sender used as the 'from' address of transferFrom, controlling whose tokens are spent and which addresses are credited.
Unchecked arithmetic values[i]*10**18 compiled with Solidity 0.6.12 (no built-in overflow protection), allowing silent multiplication overflow/truncation.
External call token.transferFrom(msg.sender, recipients[i], values[i]*10**18) executed inside a loop, with its boolean result only checked by require.

edges.reason: The function body executes the unchecked multiplication values[i]*10**18 on every loop iteration, so control flow reaches the unsafe arithmetic operation.
The function body executes the external token.transferFrom call inside its for-loop, so control flow reaches the external call site.
The function consumes the untrusted msg.sender value and forwards it as the source account of the token transfer, making the caller identity security-relevant.
The loop index i determines which element values[i] is read for the arithmetic operation.
The caller-supplied values array supplies the multiplicand for values[i]*10**18, so attacker-controlled data reaches the unchecked arithmetic.
The (possibly overflowed) result of values[i]*10**18 flows directly into the external transferFrom amount argument.
msg.sender flows into the 'from' parameter of transferFrom, so the untrusted caller decides which balance is debited.
The recipients array supplies recipients[i], the destination address of the external transferFrom call.

The external token.transferFrom call hands control to an attacker-controlled token contract which may re-enter disperseTokenSimple before the loop state settles (state changes/external interaction ordering).

normalization_plan.reason: param_token is only used as the receiver of the external transferFrom call, so it should be merged into the unsafe_transferFrom operation node.
param_recipients is only used to supply recipients[i] to the transferFrom call, so it should be merged into the unsafe_transferFrom operation node.
param_values is only used as the multiplicand in values[i]*10**18, so it should be merged into the unsafe multiplication operation node.
local_i exists solely to index values[i] for the multiplication, so it should be merged into the unsafe multiplication operation node.
